The game's first instruction, where the loader hands over. With the I/O chips banked out it copies sixteen bytes from $0AD9 into the RAM under the video chip, then, with them banked in, checks eleven bytes at $CF79 against $CF99 sixteen times over; if they ever agree it jumps to $0000 and the machine crashes. Then it wipes these first 45 bytes and carries on at $083C, so in play this code is gone. A copy-protection or tamper check: the two strings differ in an untouched load.

Cold start after the check: marks no scene as loaded ($12BB = $FF), sets the first scene of a game to 0 ($12BC), keeps the scene loader safe by copying it under the I/O area (s_6800), clears both sprite-restore counts and the two-player flag, then falls into the attract mode.
Attract mode (F1 comes here too): five lives, demo playback from the start of its script ($F7AA = 0), demo flag $12B8 set, and the title picture (scene 9) as the scene to show.
Starts a real game (F7, or fire during the attract mode, comes here): five lives, demo flag off, score cleared (s_1173), and the first scene from $12BC.

Enters scene $12B9: resets the stack, clears both screen buffers' sprite-restore lists by redrawing with nothing (s_6E23 on each), sets up the scene (s_1098) and runs the scene's own start routine through the vector at $B2. On a cold start it also fills both colour screens (s_82B5). Starts the music and the score display, then runs the main loop from $08D6.

The main loop, once per four frames. Notes the frame count, reads the controls into $12BF (the joystick in port 1 in a game; the recorded demo through s_F7DF in the attract mode, or "fire" on the title), handles the music on or off key, starts a jingle per scene ($09F9), and in the attract mode a press of fire starts a game. Space pauses: while paused only the keyboard is read. Otherwise it turns fire into a one-shot press ($12D0), runs every object's behaviour (s_0A80), waits for the screen flip, erases the sprites drawn two frames ago (s_6E23), runs the scene's per-frame routine (vector $AE), draws every object (s_0AB2), runs the scene's second routine (vector $B0), updates the high score and the score line, then asks the interrupt to show the buffer just drawn and waits until four frames have passed since the loop began.

Per scene index (0 to 9), the sound start_sound plays when the music is due to restart, 0 for none: sounds 16, 17, 18 and 24 are the four tunes (0 to 3). Index 5 (scene 6) has none, and the ending and the title (indexes 8 and 9) both take sound 16.

The raster interrupt, at line $FB, once a frame. Counts frames in $12C6, and when the main loop has asked for a flip ($12C8) shows the buffer just drawn: bank 0 with the screen at $0400 and the bitmap at $2000, or bank 1 with the screen at $6000 and the bitmap at $4000. Unless the game is paused it plays the music (s_BA09, s_BA21).
Jumps through the vector at $AE: the current scene's per-frame routine, set from the table at $1279.
Jumps through the vector at $B0: the scene's second per-frame routine, run after the objects are drawn, set from the table at $128D.
Jumps through the vector at $B2: the scene's start routine, set from the table at $1265.

Runs every object's behaviour. First counts down five timers at $12D8 (reloaded from $0AAD, so they run every 2nd to 6th call), then for each of the eleven object slots with a type in $1D,x calls the routine the type selects from $0AD9, by writing it into its own JSR at $0AA4.

High byte of run_objects' rewritten JSR operand.
Reload values of the five countdown timers at $12D8: 1 to 5.
Draws every object of the eleven slots that has a type and a visible shape (bit 7 of $54,x clear), with s_0C8A.
Finds the first object slot with no type: returns its index in Y with carry clear, or carry set when all eleven are taken.
Behaviour routine for each object type, 1 to 15 (entry 0 is not used): the two Goonies, the Fratelli, and each scene's moving things. run_objects calls the one for $1D,x.
High bytes of the handler addresses, read as $0ADA,y: object_handlers is read a word at a time from $0AD9.

Behaviour of the Goonie the player controls (type 1). While dying ($12CF) it takes no input. Reads the controls (the demo's in the attract mode, otherwise the stick through read_stick), copies up onto the fire bit so that up jumps, and keeps them in $80,x for move_object; moves it (move_object), picks its animation frame (s_0C36) and plays a splash on landing in water (s_0B98). Then a hidden check (from $0B2D): it reads the CPU port's direction register $00 and returns only if it holds $EF, the value the copy-protected loader leaves there. With any other value (the KERNAL's own is $2F) it moves the Goonie a second time and calls into the middle of the interrupt handler ($0A49), whose pulls and RTI wreck the stack: in a test with $00 set to $2F the game had corrupted the screen within four passes.
The hidden loader check: LDX #$E3 / LDA $1D,X reads $00 (the index wraps round zero page), and adding $11 gives zero only when $00 holds $EF.

Behaviour of the other Goonie (type 2). With one player, fire swaps the two Goonies' types so that the other one is controlled (a sound plays); the waiting one gets no controls but still falls and lands. With two players at once it reads port 2 and moves like the first (from $0BA9).
Plays sound $0E when the moved object is in water (rectangle kind 6) and not sinking at speed 1.
Behaviour of a dying Goonie (type 3): counts $12CF up to 16, showing shape $1C then $1D, then takes a life and restarts the scene, or ends the game when none are left.

Not called from anywhere: a behaviour routine in the style of the others that shows shape 6 plus $8B,x, holds the stick bits clear of input ($1F) and moves the object. Perhaps left from an earlier object type.
Not called from anywhere: returns carry clear when slot 0 is 8 to 15 units away from object X across (either side) and within $20 lines up or down, carry set otherwise.

Chooses a Goonie's shape for this pass from what it is doing: walking right or left (two frames each, from bit 1 of its x position), climbing (two frames from bit 2 of y), standing, or swimming in water (two frames); adds the Goonie's own base shape $8B,x.

Draws object X into the back buffer: looks up its shape ($54,x) in the shape table at $70BE, takes the one of its four pointers that the two low bits of its x choose, and draws that copy at column x/4, line y (s_6D4E). For most shapes the four pointers name one copy, which then moves a byte (eight pixels) at a time; for some they name two copies four pixels apart, or four copies two pixels apart.
Is object Y inside the box $12CA-$12CD (left, top, right, bottom)? Compares the object's position and its shape's width and height ($0FE3, $101F) with the box. Carry set if they overlap. Keeps X.

Moves object X by its velocity ($28,x across, $33,x down) and settles it against the scene's rectangles. First marks which of the eight rectangle kinds the moved object touches ($105B-$1062) and notes its direction and the stick ($80,x) in $1063-$106B; then walls stop it across (s_0F3A, s_0F4B), ladders hold it ($5F,x, $6A,x, centred by s_0F63), a ceiling stops it rising (s_0F7C) and a floor stops it falling (s_0FA5). Gravity adds one to the fall speed up to four, kind 6 slows a fall, and a jump is set up from the stick: $FB upwards with fire, sideways at two.

Centres the object on the ladder rectangle it holds (kind X), and stops it across.

Scans the whole matrix for a key and returns its matrix code (row times eight plus column) in $12C1, skipping both shift keys, or $FF for none.
Tests the eight keys the game uses, a row and column pair each from $160C, and returns the key's matrix code from $161C in $12C1, or $6F for none.

Once a pass: in the attract mode, fire on port 1 starts a game. Reads the keyboard and acts on a new key. With no scene loaded it re-enters the scene. Space pauses or resumes (PAUSED is printed, the music stops), and nothing else is read while paused; F1 goes to the attract mode, F7 starts a new game, V prints the version line "V 1 BY SES", F3 on the title switches between one and two players, S turns the music off and on, and L (shift L for player 2) turns that player's joystick a quarter turn (s_172B), showing 1L or 2L.
Out of lives: blanks the status line five times with a different character ($1726), prints GAME OVER, recolours its line, forgets the loaded scene, waits 180 frames and goes back to the attract mode.
game_over's step through the five fill characters, counting down.
The five characters game_over writes into the blank status message in turn.

Reads the stick for object X: port 1 for the first Goonie, port 2 for the second when two play at once. If that player pressed L, swaps the pairs: up and down come from left and right, left and right from down and up, as for a stick held a quarter turn round. Returns up, down, left, right and fire in bits 0 to 4, as the CIA gives them: clear for pressed.

Scene 4 (the rolling rocks, scene index 3) start: on a fresh start ($12BA clear) the three planks are back ($1978 = 3), the bell counter is at 6 ($1937) and the first rolling rock is set up in slot 2 (s_1ADB). Both Goonies at x $80 and $8A, line $26, on the top floor, the second one facing left ($8C = 8).

Scene 4 each pass. While the bell is ringing ($1928 is clear and $12DD counts down five bats) it releases a bat a pass with the bell sound (7) and closes every floor gap (s_19EB). Then, for each floor (lines $1F, $47 and $6F at x $61), a Goonie standing there opens that floor's gaps under the chain (s_1859, s_185D, s_1861). Then the flap (s_1979), the planks (s_1948), the bell (s_18E9), the floor pieces (s_187A) and the exit (s_181B).
The tunnel exit (x $14 to $1C, line $BA): with both Goonies there, scores 1,000, gives three extra lives (at most nine) and goes on to scene index 4.

Writes the filter and volume ($BF39, $BF3B) and the resonance and routing ($BF80) to the SID.

The tune player, once a frame from the interrupt. Unless the tune is stopped, counts the tempo ($BF3F) down; on each tick counts down each voice's note, releasing the gate a step before the end and reading the voice's next commands when the note is over (s_BCC4).

Reads the next note of a voice: the pitch (0 is a rest) from the frequency tables at $BF81 and $BFD5, transposed by $BA2C, then the waveform and envelope unless the voice holds; then carries on with the voice's commands (s_BD07).

Reads the voice's commands until a note: a byte with bit 7 clear is the next note, $FF ends the tune; otherwise bits 4 to 6 choose one of eight commands through the branch whose offset it writes at $BD33 from $BF6E.
